subject.title: [Bug] Flaky process cleanup in daemon mode during graceful restart

question: Should daemon restart be allowed to forcibly terminate still-running OpenClaw-owned background work after a bounded shutdown deadline, and if so, which owner boundary is responsible for preserving or explicitly abandoning in-flight state?
rationale: The report proposes configurable SIGKILL behavior, but force termination changes reliability and persistence semantics and cannot be safely selected without maintainer intent plus a verified process-ownership model.

options.title: Require a reproduction first
options.body: Collect a current-main process-tree trace and logs, then choose the narrow owning lifecycle boundary from observed behavior.

options.title: Adopt bounded owned-process cleanup
options.body: Define a documented shutdown deadline and terminate only verified daemon-owned descendants after graceful cleanup completes or times out.

options.title: Keep graceful-only shutdown
options.body: Retain the existing shutdown policy and document any intentionally detached background-process contract if the observed processes are not daemon-owned.

recommendation.title: Require a reproduction first
recommendation.body: Collect a current-main process-tree trace and logs, then choose the narrow owning lifecycle boundary from observed behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the current daemon service lifecycle and restart recovery paths.
